findings.evidence: grep -rn IsPerfPair: A.lean:248-252 `private instance : (dotProductBilin ℤ ℤ : ...).IsPerfPair := by / change (dotProductEquiv ℤ (Fin n)).toLinearMap.IsPerfPair / infer_instance` and D.lean:324-328, identical including the comment `-- \`dotProductEquiv\` has \`dotProductBilin\` as its underlying linear map by definition.`
findings.fix: Add a shared module under `SimplyConnectedRootDatum/` (e.g. `SimplyConnectedRootDatum/Basic.lean`) holding this instance once, import it from both `A.lean` and `D.lean`, and delete both local copies in this PR rather than in a follow-up.
findings.issue: The `private instance : (dotProductBilin ℤ ℤ : (Fin n → ℤ) →ₗ[ℤ] (Fin n → ℤ) →ₗ[ℤ] ℤ).IsPerfPair` is duplicated verbatim (proof and comment) from A.lean:248. It depends on no root-system theory at all — only Mathlib's `dotProductEquiv` — so it does not belong in a per-type datum file, and the copy means two global instances for the same class and pairing once both modules are imported.

findings.evidence: `typeDSimpleRoot` is defined at ClassicalTypeD.lean:423; the proof at D.lean:200-211 uses only `Fintype.linearIndependent_iff`, `dotProduct_sum` and `typeDDoubleCoweight`, nothing private to ClassicalTypeD and nothing from `RootDatum`. ClassicalTypeD.lean's own docstring states it gives "the concrete infrastructure needed to build its pinned integral root datum", which is where this PR already placed `typeDSimpleRootCoordinates_nonneg_or_nonpos` (ClassicalTypeD.lean:891).
findings.fix: Move `typeDDoubleCoweight` (D.lean:179), `typeDDoubleCoweight_dotProduct_typeDSimpleRoot` (D.lean:185) and `linearIndependent_typeDSimpleRoot` into `ClassicalTypeD.lean` next to `typeDSimpleRoot`, updating its module docstring's declaration list; keep the datum-specific `two_mul_typeDSimpleRootCoordinates` wherever it is most convenient after the move.
findings.issue: `linearIndependent_typeDSimpleRoot` is public and stated entirely in the classical model's vocabulary (`LinearIndependent ℤ (typeDSimpleRoot n hn)`), with no reference to the root datum. Its subject `typeDSimpleRoot` is defined in the earlier `ClassicalTypeD.lean:423`, so any other consumer of the classical type D model must import the simply connected datum to obtain it.

summary: The new file is in the right subdirectory and every import is used, but a general-purpose IsPerfPair instance is copy-pasted verbatim from A.lean instead of shared, and a public theorem stated purely in the classical model's vocabulary sits in the datum file rather than in ClassicalTypeD.lean.
